subject: Re: DPA proposal for hybrid deployment — subprocessor & cross-border clarifications
messages:
From: Emily Jordan <emily.jordan@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luca Bianchi <luca.bianchi@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: DPA for hybrid deployment (Dedicated + VPC)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team asked me to follow up on a few items before we can move to a pilot contract: specifically how Redwood's DPA handles (a) subprocessors for hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, and (b) cross-border transfers for customer data collected in the EU / UK.

High level asks:
- A current list of subprocessors with roles and locations for each deployment mode.
- Confirmation whether Redwood treats Dedicated capacity differently from Private (VPC/on-prem) in the DPA (data processing scope, liability, audit access).
- Any model for data localization or guarantees for EU-only processing.
- Whether Redwood will sign SCCs and the approach for EEA -> US transfers.

We're gating this before procurement pushes the PO. Can you loop in your privacy/compliance contact and send over a draft DPA or your standard language?

Appreciate it,
Emily Jordan
Sr. Counsel, Acme HealthTech
attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Jordan <emily.jordan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA for hybrid deployment (Dedicated + VPC)

Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (privacy lead), Marissa (account lead), and Karthik (deployment/product) to give authoritative answers. Short answers up front:

- Subprocessors: we maintain a single canonical subprocessors list that maps subprocessors to functions (hosting, monitoring, telemetry, analytics). The list is the same across modes, but the degree of access and legal boundary differs (we mark whether a subprocessor handles customer content or only telemetry/infra).
- Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem): Private/VPC gives the customer control over networks and often keys; our DPA includes a clause that limits Redwood's access to customer data for on-prem installs. Dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud) is still processed by Redwood-managed infrastructure and so remains subject to the full DPA + subprocessors list.
- SCCs: We will execute SCCs and support EEA->US transfers using the standard SCC addendum. We also offer technical controls (encryption in transit + at rest, customer KMS integration on Private) to reduce transfer risk.

Rishi — can you confirm the latest white‑label subprocessors CSV and whether we should provide a scoped list specific to Acme's pilot?

Emily — attaching our current DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Hybrid_Deployment_v2.docx). We'll review Acme's redlines if you send them back.

Next steps:
1) Rishi to share subprocessors export and call out any processors that would change if Acme selects Private on‑prem.
2) We can provide SCC addendum draft + proposed wording for restricted access for Private deployments.
3) If acceptable, we'll prepare DocuSign envelope for signature.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_DPA_Hybrid_Deployment_v2.docx (DPA draft)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA for hybrid deployment (Dedicated + VPC)

Hannah / team —

Uploading the current subprocessors summary for hybrid deployments (exported). Key points to call out:
- Core infra (hosting): our cloud provider (multi-region), located in US, EU, APAC — will appear on the list with the role 'hosting'.
- Observability & metrics: our telemetry vendor has access to aggregated logs only; we flag this as non-customer-content access.
- Model repo & caching: third-party cache layer is in the US; if a customer requires on‑prem, that component is not used.
- Data access: for Private (VPC) deployments, by default we do not ingest customer PII into our hosted control plane — we can add a contractual data flow diagram and a clause that prohibits Redwood from retrieving customer content without documented escalation (customer-managed support ticket + JIT access logged).

I've attached the subprocessors export as a CSV to the thread (refer to the Doc name in Drive). If Acme needs a narrower list scoped to the pilot (e.g., exclude analytics vendors), we can provide that under an NDA.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: subprocessors_hybrid_export.csv (drive link in related_links)
From: Luca Bianchi <luca.bianchi@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Emily Jordan <emily.jordan@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:36:00 +0000
Subject: Acme redlines: DPA (attached)

Hannah —

Please find Acme's consolidated redlines attached (Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf). Summary of the material asks from our side:
1) Add explicit language that for Private (on‑prem / VPC) deployments, Redwood will not transfer customer content outside designated regions unless the customer provides explicit written consent.
2) Narrow subprocessors: require notice + 30-day right to object for any new subprocessor that would handle customer content.
3) Audit rights: request on‑site or remote SOC2 evidence and for Private deployments the right to audit on‑prem components under strict protocol.
4) Data retention: retention periods aligned to Acme's policy (30 days for request logs, 180 days for KVs — proposal attached).

Can Rishi confirm which of these are acceptable and which would need exceptions? We are aiming to close the DPA by EOD next Friday so procurement can route the PO.

Thanks,
Luca Bianchi
Head of InfoSec Operations | Acme HealthTech
attachments: Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Jordan <emily.jordan@acmehealth.com>, Luca Bianchi <luca.bianchi@acmehealth.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme redlines: DPA (attached)

Luca / Emily —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Quick responses from Redwood: 
- Region‑locking for Private/VPC: we can accept language that prevents transfers outside designated regions for Private deployments provided the deployment is configured in that regional boundary and Acme manages the keys (KMS) or we use an approved customer-managed KMS. For Dedicated (reserved capacity), we can offer region-specific Dedicated pools scoped to EU only for an enterprise commitment.
- Subprocessor notice & objection: we can provide 30 days' notice and a right to object that escalates to a contractual review. We can carve out emergency security subprocessors that may need accelerated onboarding with post‑notice.
- Audit rights: we can provide SOC2 reports and a remote audit protocol for Private deployments; limited on‑site audit rights can be discussed but will need a scoped MOU that addresses confidentiality and operational safety.
- Retention windows: we will propose a compromise retention schedule and make retention configurable at deployment.

I'll prepare a tracked-copy of our DPA that incorporates the above and flags the narrow exceptions (emergency subprocessors, scoped on‑site audits). If that aligns, we'll route the DocuSign envelope.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

- Added a Private/VPC region-locking clause when customer chooses Private and uses customer-managed keys.

- Provided SOC2 remote audit protocol and proposed MOU language for any limited on‑site audits.

Best,
